summary: Site structure is sound: build reproducibility, all internal anchors/hrefs, tab navigation, data-prose consistency (72 WINs / 19 acknowledged failures), progressive-disclosure structure, discoverability infrastructure, and all pipeline-continuity checks (expansion tracker, ISS-id collisions, FUSE-vs-git prompt staleness, workspace-only files, digest coverage, broken reviews, drift audit, curmudgeon-dispatcher-state, Mech-A-bypass audit, delete-propagation backlog, status.json provenance, ownership-registration-gap) came back clean; test.js is 3885/3885 green, and the live published site's content signature matches git HEAD exactly (pages_freshness: FRESH). External-link checking is skipped today per the weekly-Monday cadence. The one real story this run surfaces is operational, not structural: this integrity check, and every other dome-* scheduled agent, currently shows enabled=false in the live scheduler, despite each having run once earlier today -- almost certainly a manual catch-up following the documented 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-25/26 pipeline outage (confirmed independently by decider's own 'first run post-39d-outage' commit and by ISS-3091). Unless the operator explicitly re-enables the scheduled tasks, the pipeline will go silent again starting tomorrow. Two minor items for the analyst's list: WIN-070 didn't turn up in a text-search cross-check against the dome's live wins.html (likely a check limitation, not a real removal), and the published date banner is ~40 days stale (cosmetic only, content itself verified current). overall_status is set to 'fail' solely to route the scheduler-disabled finding to alerts.txt for urgent operator attention -- no site-structural or data check actually failed this run.
